data.name: Freakshow:Anniversary
data.detailed_description:
Freakshow came out originally August 2017! This is to celebrate the anniversary of the project!

You go visit the local circus and he takes you. What will you discover?


Major updates compared to the original (2017):
-Achievements
-Original soundtrack!
-Inventory system
-Better voice acting
-And more!


Come play a few puzzles and enjoy the mini games!

Thank you for supporting this game through the development!

reviews.review:
Freakshow:Anniversary is a compact indie adventure built around the unsettling atmosphere of a local circus and the mystery of what might be hiding behind its attractions. Developed and published by KevinTheWolfy, it was created as an anniversary celebration of the original Freakshow project from 2017. Instead of completely reinventing the concept, this edition expands on the earlier version with additional features and improvements, resulting in a strange mixture of casual adventure, horror, puzzle solving, exploration, and minigames. Its limited production values are apparent, but the unusual setting and personal nature of the project give it an identity of its own.

The story begins with the player visiting a circus, with the seemingly ordinary trip developing into a more mysterious experience. Much of the appeal comes from discovering what the circus contains rather than following an elaborate narrative introduction. This approach suits the game's dark atmosphere because uncertainty becomes part of the experience. The circus theme provides a useful contrast between entertainment and discomfort, allowing colorful or playful ideas to exist alongside horror elements and mature material. It is more interested in creating an odd, unpredictable mood than delivering relentless scares.

Gameplay combines exploration with puzzles and several minigames. One of the notable improvements over the original project is the inventory system, which gives the adventure a more traditional point-and-click flavor. Finding items and determining where they belong adds some structure to progression, while puzzles encourage players to pay attention to their surroundings. The minigames introduce additional variety and help prevent the experience from becoming entirely dependent on walking around and examining objects. None of these individual mechanics are exceptionally deep, but together they create a reasonably varied structure for such a small game.

The anniversary treatment also introduces Steam achievements, with 13 available to collect. This gives completion-focused players additional objectives beyond simply reaching the end of the adventure. Multiple-ending elements further encourage experimentation and replaying portions of the experience. Players interested in uncovering every secret may therefore get more mileage from the game than someone who simply follows the most direct route through it. Exploration remains one of its more important qualities, particularly because discovering unusual situations is central to the circus premise.

Audio received additional attention for this version, including an original soundtrack and improved voice acting. These are worthwhile enhancements because atmosphere is especially important in a horror-themed adventure with modest visuals. Music helps establish the strange personality of the circus, while voice acting gives the characters and situations more presence. The visual presentation remains relatively simple and unmistakably indie, so players accustomed to polished commercial horror games should adjust their expectations. The roughness can occasionally work in the game's favor by making the world feel even stranger, although it can just as easily expose the project's technical limitations.

The experience is designed entirely around single-player play and supports English interface and full audio. Its hardware requirements are exceptionally lightweight, requiring only 2 GB of RAM, a basic 2 GHz-class processor, DirectX 11, and roughly 400 MB of storage. The current Windows requirements specify Windows 10 or 11. This means most reasonably modern PCs should have little difficulty meeting the listed specifications. Being free to play is another major advantage, since players can investigate its peculiar circus adventure without having to make a financial commitment.

Steam Deck compatibility is not officially confirmed. The game does not currently carry a clear Steam Deck Verified or Playable classification, so it is best regarded as Unverified for Deck use. Its modest hardware demands suggest that raw performance should not be the primary concern, but performance requirements and actual Steam Deck compatibility are different matters. Controls, interface behavior, runtime compatibility, and other factors can affect the handheld experience. Anyone specifically intending to play on Steam Deck should therefore expect that manual adjustments or compatibility-layer experimentation could potentially be necessary.

Freakshow:Anniversary does have weaknesses that are difficult to overlook. Its gameplay systems are fairly basic, the presentation lacks the refinement of larger adventure games, and the combination of horror, puzzles, casual minigames, strategy elements, and exploration can sometimes feel more like a collection of ideas than a tightly unified design. The Steam user reception being in the Mixed range reflects how divisive this type of small experimental project can be. Players expecting sophisticated puzzles, extensive storytelling, polished animation, or genuinely intense survival horror will probably find it too limited.

Despite those shortcomings, there is something appealing about seeing an older personal project revisited and expanded rather than abandoned. The addition of achievements, inventory mechanics, improved voice work, an original soundtrack, puzzles, and minigames demonstrates an effort to turn the original concept into a more complete experience. Its free-to-play availability also makes its rough edges easier to forgive. Freakshow:Anniversary is most suitable for players who enjoy obscure indie horror, unconventional point-and-click adventures, and small experimental games where personality matters more than technical sophistication. It is imperfect and occasionally awkward, but its strange circus atmosphere and assortment of ideas make it an interesting curiosity for the right audience.

Rating: 5/10
